title: ops-shift-chronicle-latency-triage-2029-10-02
body:
Shift chronicle: latency triage and on-call handoff notes

Window: 2029-09-30 00:00 UTC -> 2029-10-02 11:30 UTC
Authors: Aisha (primary on-call), Marco (shift support), Leah (runtime eng), Samir (infra)

Summary (top-line)
- High-level: We observed two capacity-related latency spikes that pushed model-serving p99 above SLO during peak US-EAST traffic on 2029-10-01 17:24 UTC and again at 2029-10-02 03:06 UTC.
- Impact: API p99 target (250ms) breached to ~420ms for 13 minutes in first event and ~310ms for 7 minutes in second event. Error rate stayed below alert thresholds; no customer-reported data loss.
- Current status: Follow-ups opened; temporary mitigations applied; handoff to next on-call completed.

Incident timeline (concise)
- 2029-10-01 17:24 UTC: Pager alert SRE-PAGE-847 triggered for p99 latency > 300ms for 5m across hosted-api route /v1/generate.
- 17:25:30 UTC: On-call (Aisha) joins bridge, confirms spike correlates with sustained burst of model-inference requests to m-neo-13B quantized variant.
- 17:27 UTC: Tracing shows increased kernel queue wait on gpul-nodeset-3 and KV cache miss rate jump from 4% -> 28%.
- 17:33 UTC: Autoscaler started adding pods but observed slow warmup due to KV cache population (cold cache per shard).
- 17:37 UTC: Applied mitigation: route low-priority traffic to model-variant m-neo-13B-cached (prewarmed pool) and raised batch size cap per-request to reduce per-token overhead.
- 17:37-17:40 UTC: p99 slid back down toward SLO over three minutes.
- 2029-10-02 03:06 UTC: Second, smaller spike; traced to a periodic background job that rebuilt shard routing table (INFRA-523) causing transient misrouting and simultaneous cache invalidation on a subset of nodes.
- 03:10 UTC: Disabled job schedule until fix; rerouted traffic similarly; spike ended by 03:13 UTC.

Root cause (current hypothesis)
- Primary: KV cache thrashing due to simultaneous cache invalidation + autoscaler-induced cold starts. The runtime reacts to unexpected shard mapping updates by evicting or reinitializing local KV caches which increases token generation latency while caches warm.
- Secondary: Background routing table job (INFRA-523) runs without a staggered rollout; when it coincided with a traffic burst it amplified cold-start effects.
- Contributing: Some prewarm thresholds in the dedicated pool are too conservative for sudden bursts (see PR #1217 for prewarm tuning suggestions).

Detection and instrumentation notes
- Traces: span duration increased for "kv-lookup" and "attention-kernel-wait" spans.
- Metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate, node_kernel_queue_length, model_warmup_seconds. We need a dashboard that overlays kv_cache_hit_rate with autoscaler events.
- Alert tuning: current p99 alert is noisy for transient cold starts. Consider adding a secondary alert for kv_cache_miss_rate > 20% sustained for 3m.

Mitigations applied during shift
- Emergency routing: routed 25% of lower-priority traffic to the warm pool variant (manual override).
- Temporarily paused INFRA-523 job schedule (rolling back to earlier mapping).
- Increase prewarm threshold for m-neo-13B-cached from 2 -> 4 instances per shard in US-EAST (tweak via infra feature flag).
- Opened immediate PR to extend warmup grace window for autoscaler (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1217).

Customer impact
- No escalations opened by CS during window. A few high-usage customers saw slower responses; automated monitoring flagged increased tail latency but no 5xx spikes.
- We will proactively email top-10 latency-sensitive tenants with a short summary if follow-up fixes extend into next week.

On-call handoff notes
- Outgoing on-call: Aisha P. (shift ends 2029-10-02 11:30 UTC). Incoming: Marco R.
- Active follow-ups transferred: SRE-2981 (investigate KV eviction pattern), INFRA-523 (stagger routing job), INFRA-5435 (dashboard for kv cache + autoscaler overlay).
- Playbook pointers: see playbook "kv-cache-coldstart" on Confluence (pageId 824915). Steps to re-route are in the "emergency-routing" runbook.
- Contact list: Leah Chen (runtime lead) mobile +1-415-555-0131; Samir Gupta (infra) pager on-call.

Action items and owners (short)
- SRE-2981 (assigned Aisha): Pull long-term histogram of kv_cache_hit_rate by shard and node, include correlation with autoscaler events. Due 2029-10-09.
- INFRA-523 (assigned Samir): Implement staggered routing-table rollout and circuit-breaker for job. Due 2029-10-08.
- RTE-4020 (assigned Leah): Add prewarm health probe and increase default warm instances for quantized models. Due 2029-10-10.
- MON-2210 (assigned Marco): Build combined dashboard and add alert for kv_cache_miss_rate > 20% sustained for 3m. Due 2029-10-07.

Quick wins we applied (notes to self)
- Short-term: Manual warm pool routing handled 2x of expected burst load; consider automating fallback policy for warm pools.
- Low-effort: Increase autoscaler warmup delay to 45s to prevent premature acceptance of traffic. Patch in infra flags repo minimal risk.

Open questions / discussion items for weekly sync
- How aggressive should autoscaler prewarm be for quantized vs non-quantized models? Trade-offs: cost vs tail latency.
- Do we want a dedicated warm-only pool for top-10 latency-critical customers? Pricing/ops implications?
- Should routing-table jobs always run with a staged rollout and health checks per shard (yes, but need implementer)?

Appendix: Helpful logs and links
- Top traces (examples): trace ids T-7f4a9, T-7f4b2 (attached to ticket SRE-2981).
- Relevant PRs and tickets: SRE-2981, INFRA-523, RTE-4020, MON-2210.
- Slack threads: #ops-bridge-pin-2029-10-01, #latency-debug (see linked_artifacts list).

Retro notes (what worked / what did not)
- Worked: route fallback to warm pool + quick rollback of routing job prevented longer outage. Communication on bridge was fast; CS informed within 12 mins.
- Did not work: no single-pane dashboard showing kv cache + autoscaler events; playbook step to "check warm-pool capacity" was ambiguous.

Closing: Handoff completed, follow-ups assigned. Next on-call will prioritize MON-2210 + staggered rollout for INFRA-523 before next high-traffic window.

Draft end.

Notes to self (informal)
- Remember to add step in playbook to check for concurrent infra jobs before making scaling changes.
- Put a simple runbook for "pause non-critical background jobs" on a single button in console.

-- Aisha
